question: After two galaxies merge, why can their central black holes stall for ages a few light years apart?
answer: Because they run out of stars to throw. The pair sinks by flinging passing stars away, each carrying off some orbital energy, and soon the nearby stars are gone. Gravitational waves only take over much closer in. In 2023, pulsar-timing arrays reported a background hum of such waves: a sign that pairs do get through.
move: A process that feeds on its surroundings stalls when it has used them up.
reference: Begelman, Blandford & Rees, Massive black hole binaries in active galactic nuclei, Nature, 1980
